title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN)
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence; British Thoracic Society; Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network
journal: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NICE guideline NG245, published 27 November 2024
result: Do not prescribe short-acting beta2 agonists to people of any age with asthma without a concomitant prescription of an inhaled corticosteroid. Offer a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid/formoterol inhaler taken as needed (anti-inflammatory reliever, AIR, therapy) to people aged 12 and over with newly diagnosed asthma, and change people with confirmed asthma who use a short-acting beta2 agonist only to as-needed AIR therapy. For children aged 5 to 11 years with newly diagnosed asthma, offer twice-daily paediatric low-dose inhaled corticosteroid with a short-acting beta2 agonist as needed. In November 2025 only certain budesonide/formoterol inhalers were licensed for as-needed AIR therapy in mild asthma, and the supporting evidence came from a dry powder inhaler.
